main_text.l: Poëtarum aliquo, & Sententias ex Oratoribus, intertexunt & Adagia: Ubicumque, etiam ex rebus levissimis captant occasionem hæc in medium producendi: Imo non sumunt occasionem ex rebus, sed adferunt: Verbi gratia, in Logica de-Individuo forte agentes, in Exemplum adducent Alexandrum & Bucephalum, quasi Petrus & Paulus, qui ad pedes eorum assident, illi muneri obeundo non sint pares: Et mox (quasi reseratâ jam in RHAPSODIAM fenestrâ) hic, inquiunt, est ille Alexander Philippi, qui tot Persarum exercitus delevit, & totum Orientem suo subjugavit imperio: Bucephalus autem est equus ferocissimus, quem ille puer etiamnum domuit, quo facto Philippus ei, præsagiendo spoponderat Orbis imperium: Atque ita passim corradunt ex Veterum

page.notes: The facing page's right-hand margin is very faint and partly cut off; no note text was legible enough to record. "Individuo" and the Greek-free text are as printed; "spoponderat" is printed with a long s and is kept as shown.
